finding.claim: The DELETE /reports/:id handler calls the async authorize() without await. The 403 rejection is never observed, so db.reports.remove() runs whether or not the user has the 'delete' grant. Any caller can delete any report. The rejected promise is also unhandled, which on Node 15+ can crash the process.
finding.source: Any request to DELETE /reports/:id. The attacker only needs a session whose user lacks the 'delete' grant on the target report, and can choose any report id.
finding.sink: db.reports.remove(report.id) at server.js:21, the protected delete operation.

trace.note: The report is fetched by the attacker-controlled req.params.id.
authorize(...) is not awaited or returned. The async function runs db.grants() and throws the 403 inside a promise that nothing consumes.
db.reports.remove(report.id) runs immediately, without waiting for the authorization result.
The handler returns 204, so the attacker sees the delete succeed.

finding.guards_checked: The authorize() implementation is correct (server.js:9-16), and the PUT handler at line 27 awaits it properly, so only DELETE is bypassed. No other middleware does authorization. The global middleware at lines 4-7 only copies req.session.user. No try/catch, no error middleware, and no unhandledRejection handler exist. The route is public ingress, since app.listen(3003) binds on all interfaces.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws a 403 on a missing grant, but the DELETE handler at line 20 calls it without await, so the throw is never observed. The global middleware at lines 4-7 only copies the session user. There is no try/catch, error middleware or unhandledRejection handler.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls authorize() without await, so db.reports.remove() at server.js:21 runs regardless of the grant check. Any authenticated user can therefore delete any report, and the PUT handler at line 27 shows the correct awaited form. The attacker only needs a session, which the middleware at lines 4-7 requires, but does not need the 'delete' grant.

finding.claim: The PUT /reports/:id handler passes the whole request body to db.reports.update() with no field allowlist (mass assignment). A user with only the 'write' grant can overwrite protected fields such as owner, id or ACL/grant fields, if the schema has them. Whether those fields exist depends on the db layer, which is not in this repo, so this is plausible but unconfirmed.
finding.source: The JSON body of PUT /reports/:id from a user who holds the 'write' grant.

trace.note: authorize() checks only the 'write' action on the resource, not which fields may be changed.
req.body is passed to update() unfiltered.

finding.guards_checked: No schema validation or field allowlist is present. The db implementation is not in the repo, so I could not check for model-level protection.

verdict.reason: server.js:28 passes req.body unfiltered to db.reports.update() after only the 'write' check at server.js:27 (properly awaited, so it works), but `db` is not defined anywhere in the repo, so I can't tell whether owner/ACL fields exist or are protected.
